Run as the leader under a Kubernetes Lease

Source: R/leader_election.R
run_as_leader.Rd

Acquire-and-renew leader election against a coordination.k8s.io/v1 Lease object. At most one caller across a cluster holds the lease at a time; leadership passes to another caller when the holder stops renewing (within lease_duration_seconds).

Usage

run_as_leader(
  client,
  lease_name,
  lease_namespace,
  identity,
  on_started_leading,
  on_stopped_leading = function() NULL,
  on_new_leader = NULL,
  lease_duration_seconds = 15,
  renew_deadline_seconds = 10,
  retry_period_seconds = 2,
  release_on_exit = TRUE
)

Arguments

client

An ApiClient.

lease_name

Name of the Lease object (created if missing).

lease_namespace

Namespace of the Lease.

identity

Unique identifier for this caller (hostname + PID is a common choice). Two callers with the same identity are considered the same holder and will never contest each other.

on_started_leading

Function called once when this caller acquires the lease, with a leader handle (see Details) as its only argument.

on_stopped_leading

Function called once, with no arguments, when this caller loses the lease (always paired with on_started_leading).

on_new_leader

Optional function(identity) called whenever the observed leader changes (including this caller becoming leader).

lease_duration_seconds

How long a successful acquire is valid (default 15s). Other callers will consider the lease expired after this interval of no renewal.

renew_deadline_seconds

How long to keep trying to renew before giving up and calling on_stopped_leading (default 10s).

retry_period_seconds

Interval between acquire attempts and between renewals (default 2s).

release_on_exit

Release the lease when leadership ends, so a successor does not have to wait for it to expire (default TRUE).

Requires lease_duration_seconds > renew_deadline_seconds > retry_period_seconds, as in client-go.

Value

Invisibly, TRUE once this caller has held and given up leadership.

Details

Mirrors kubernetes.leaderelection.LeaderElection (Python) and client-go/tools/leaderelection.

run_as_leader() blocks until the lease is acquired, then starts a background renewer (a callr child process) and calls on_started_leading(leader). Because R cannot interrupt running code from another thread, your callback must check in periodically by calling leader$check(). It returns invisibly while this caller is still the leader and signals a condition of class rk8s_leadership_lost once leadership is gone (the lease was taken over, or no renewal has succeeded within renew_deadline_seconds). run_as_leader() catches that condition. leader$is_leader() returns the same information as a logical.

When the callback returns, errors, or loses leadership, the renewer is stopped, the lease is released (so a successor can take over immediately, unless release_on_exit = FALSE), and on_stopped_leading() is called. Errors other than lost leadership are re-raised after this cleanup.

A callback that takes no arguments is still supported, but it then has no way to learn that leadership was lost while it runs.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
client <- new_client_from_config()
run_as_leader(
  client,
  lease_name = "my-controller",
  lease_namespace = "kube-system",
  identity = paste0(Sys.info()[["nodename"]], "-", Sys.getpid()),
  on_started_leading = function(leader) {
    repeat {
      leader$check()          # returns, or unwinds once leadership is lost
      reconcile_once()
      Sys.sleep(1)
    }
  },
  on_stopped_leading = function() message("stopped leading")
)
} # }
